extracted.intended_audience: members of the Royal Society, 17th‑century natural philosophers, and learned readers
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting evaluative principles and reporting standards implicit or explicit in the 1665 Philosophical Transactions (introduction, accounts, and lists of experiments). The page contains editorial intentions, examples of observational and experimental practice, and a numbered plan of an experimental work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: “it was intended, for the advancement of science and the benefit of mankind, to make known to the world ... the results of the labours”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication should aim to advance natural knowledge and benefit mankind by making the results of scientific labours known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusivity of contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: “not only of those persons who were members of this Society, but also of other learned men, in this and other countries”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributions may come from society members and learned men domestically and abroad; the journal accepts and disseminates work from multiple countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate to stimulate further work
rubrics_metrics.description: “that by the communication of such discoveries others might be stimulated and encouraged to similar exertions”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should be communicated in a way that enables and encourages replication, follow‑up, or extension by other investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize papers in a stated order
rubrics_metrics.description: “Mr. Oldenburg then enters immediately on the memoirs or papers themselves; which are presented in the following order:”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journal content should be arranged in a clear, declared order (table of contents / organized presentation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an ephemeris with daily positions and times
rubrics_metrics.description: “exhibiting an ephemeris, in which he determines for every day its place in the heavens, the hour of its coming to the meridian, and that of its setting”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Astronomical reports/predictions should give daily positional data and times (meridian transit, setting) so others can locate and verify the object.

rubrics_metrics.name: State modeling assumptions clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: “This ephemeris is founded on the supposition of its moving justly enough in the plane of a great circle, inclined to the equinoctial about 30°, and to the ecliptic about 49° or 49§°, cutting the equator at about 45°”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must state the assumptions and geometric/model foundations underlying their calculations or ephemerides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show methods and calculations so motion can be traced
rubrics_metrics.description: “Then M. Auzout proceeds to show how the motion of this comet is to be traced on the globe, and to calculate the several places of its appearance in the heavens”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide step‑by‑step methods and calculations enabling others to trace predicted motions on instruments (e.g., globe) and reproduce results.

rubrics_metrics.name: List chief experimental heads (structuring an experimental work)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The chief heads of this work are,” followed by a numbered list of experiments and observations (see subsequent entries)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An experimental study should be organized under clear, enumerated heads/topics describing the questions and types of experiments undertaken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments touching bodies capable of freezing others
rubrics_metrics.description: “Experiments touching bodies capable of freezing others.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As listed by Boyle as a primary experimental topic to be addressed in a systematic study of cold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments and observations touching bodies disposed to be frozen
rubrics_metrics.description: “Experiments and observations touching bodies disposed to be frozen.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document which bodies tend to freeze and report observations systematically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments touching bodies indisposed to be frozen
rubrics_metrics.description: “Experiments touching bodies indisposed to be frozen.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report and analyze materials that resist freezing as a distinct experimental category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments and observations touching the degrees of cold in several bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: “Experiments and observations touching the degrees of cold in several bodies.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and compare degrees/amounts of cold across different substances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments touching the tendency of cold upwards or downwards
rubrics_metrics.description: “Experiments touching the tendency of cold upwards or downwards.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate and report directional behavior of cold (e.g., whether cold rises or sinks) with controlled experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments and observations touching the preservation and destruction of eggs, apples, and other bodies by cold
rubrics_metrics.description: “Experiments and observations touching the preservation and destruction of eggs, apples, and other bodies by cold.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include applied/biological effects of cold (preservation/destruction) in systematic tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments touching the expansion of water and aqueous liquors by freezing
rubrics_metrics.description: “Experiments touching the expansion of water and aqueous liquors by freezing.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify volumetric expansion on freezing and report experimental method and measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments touching the contraction of liquors by cold
rubrics_metrics.description: “Experiments touching the contraction of liquors by cold.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure contraction effects and include methods and data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments in consort touching the bubbles, from which the levity of ice is supposed to proceed
rubrics_metrics.description: “Experiments in consort, touching the bubbles, from which the levity of ice is supposed to proceed.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group experiments addressing hypothesized mechanisms (here, bubbles causing ice’s levity) and report coordinated findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments about the measure of expansion and contraction of liquors by cold
rubrics_metrics.description: “Experiments about the measure of the expansion and the contraction of liquors by cold.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide measurements/metrics for expansion and contraction; include methods for estimating magnitudes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments touching differing mediums through which cold may be diffused
rubrics_metrics.description: “Experiments and observations touching the sphere of activity of cold.” / “Experiments touching differing mediums through which cold may be diffused.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine the range/sphere of cold’s activity and how different media transmit or insulate cold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments and observations touching ice and snow duration/destruction
rubrics_metrics.description: “Experiments and observations touching ice.” / “Experiments and observations touching the duration of ice and snow, and the destroying of them by air, and several liquors.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate persistence and melting/destruction mechanisms for ice and snow under various agents (air, liquids).

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations and experiments on the primum frigidum
rubrics_metrics.description: “Considerations and experiments touching the primum frigidum.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss and test the primary cause/essence of cold (primum frigidum) via experiment and argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments and observations touching the coldness and temperature of the air
rubrics_metrics.description: “Experiments and observations touching the coldness and temperature of the air.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure air temperature and analyze its properties as a distinct experimental subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report strange effects and weight changes from freezing
rubrics_metrics.description: “Of the strange effects of cold.” / “Experiments touching the weight of bodies frozen and unfrozen.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record anomalous phenomena and perform comparative weight measurements on frozen vs unfrozen samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include promiscuous/ancillary experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: “Promiscuous experiments and observations concerning cold.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record miscellaneous but relevant observations and experiments that do not fit neatly into other heads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optical instrument performance standards
rubrics_metrics.description: “he uses three eye-glasses for his great telescopes, without finding any Iris, or such rain-bow colours, as usually appear in ordinary glasses, and prove an impediment to observations.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optical designs should minimize chromatic/‘rain‑bow’ colour effects that impede observations; report lens construction and observed artefacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large telescope quality claim
rubrics_metrics.description: “it having hitherto been found by experience, that small glasses are in proportion better to see with, on the earth, than large ones; that author affirms, that his are equally good for the earth, and for making observations in the heavens.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims about instrument improvements (e.g., large lenses performing as well as small) should be reported and justified by observation and description of construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeated timed observations to demonstrate motion
rubrics_metrics.description: “he had ... observed ... a small spot ... and that, observing it from time to time, he found, that within two hours after, the said spot had moved from east to west, about half the length of the diameter of Jupiter.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document repeated observations with precise time references to demonstrate temporal changes (motion) of features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test instruments under operational conditions and compare to established methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Account of pendulum watches: he adjusted his watches, sailed, and compared watch‑based reckonings to pilots' journals and calculations, finding disagreement among pilots but agreement with the watches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate instruments in realistic operational contexts (e.g., at sea), compare results against existing practices/judgements, and report discrepancies and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide detailed physical measurements and descriptions in natural history accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The whale‑fishing account gives lengths, tail breadth, fin lengths, gill lengths, descriptions of shape, colour, internal contents (greenish grassy matter), and oil properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural history/narrative reports should include explicit measurements, morphology, and material/chemical observations to allow assessment and comparison.
